acme_dev: Hey @support, streaming API cut off for our workflow — last event contains an unterminated JSON object and no finish_reason. We see:
```
data: {"id":"resp_123","chunks":[{"text":"Hello"},{"text":" world"}],"meta":{"seq":2}
```
then connection closes. This kills our parser (we rely on finish_reason). Repro from our side: node-fetch streaming reconnect -> resume token present. Happens ~3x/day since yesterday after our billing token rotated. env: prod, eu-west1, client: node 18, using fetch keepalive false. Any ideas?

support_jen: thanks — can you paste the exact curl you used and the sequence of headers on reconnect?

acme_dev: curl we used:
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME-OLD" \
 -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
 https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=gpt-lite \
 -o /tmp/stream.log
```
on reconnect we send "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME-NEW" and `x-resume-token: abc123`. logs show 200 then abrupt EOF. shipping log: attached snippet (paste). Not seeing 401.

raj_sre: assign to eng-runtime to look at resume handshake. @ingrid_runtime can you grab proxy/backend logs for that timeslice?

ingrid_runtime: looking. Fastly edge shows backend returned chunked stream, then connection reset by peer from upstream after 12s of inactivity. Backend (inference-runtime) logs show:
"stream-session 789 closing - no finisher emitted - resume_token abc123"
that means runtime closed connection before final sentinel. Putting more logs here:
`[2026-03-01T14:03:12Z] kvcache: save ok`
`[2026-03-01T14:03:12Z] stream: no more tokens, closing stream without final event`
looks like auth rotation triggered a soft-stop path that didn't emit the terminal event.

tyler_devex: thought the runtime always emits `event: done
data: {"finish_reason":"stop"}` before close. Is there a codepath where auth refresh causes an abrupt stop?

ingrid_runtime: yes, there's a path where the loop calls `close_stream()` on token change before final flush if `auth_changed=true`. We saw it in a recent patch but not triggered in tests.

support_jen: customer needs a workaround now — can they set client to wait+retry and accept partial results?

acme_dev: Not ideal. Our product needs terminated JSON. Any quick mitigation?

raj_sre: short-term: add an intermediate resume step — on reconnect, call `GET /v1/stream/resume?token=abc123` which forces server to send the final object if available. We can add this endpoint as a temporary shim. @ingrid_runtime any objections?

ingrid_runtime: I can spin up a hotfix to ensure `close_stream()` always emits terminal event before closing, plus backup route `/resume` to emit missing sentinel when state present. Will prep patch and rollout to a small canary.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary group=eu-west1-r1 - rollout id d-5543

acme_dev: thanks. Quick question: could Fastly or TLS handshake be dropping the last bytes? we saw network logs with FIN after upstream EOF.

ingrid_runtime: possible, but logs show runtime didn't write the final event. Repro steps I've used:
1) start stream with auth A
2) midstream rotate auth to B (simulate /auth/rotate)
3) trigger runtime reeval -> codepath early-close without terminal event
4) client reconnect with `x-resume-token` and sees no `done` existing -> parser stuck

Code snippet to reproduce locally:
```
# pseudo
connect_stream(auth=A)
yield "Hello"
rotate_auth(auth=B)
runtime_close(no_terminal=true)
client_reconnect(resume_token)
```

tyler_devex: for customer-facing workaround add an SSE-safe client: treat EOF as implicit finish after a short grace (e.g., 750ms) if no finish_reason present and attempt resume once. Add note in docs.

support_jen: documenting workaround and ETA for fix. ETA for hotfix?

ingrid_runtime: hotfix PR ready, running unit + integ. Canary in 15m, full deploy in 2 hours if green.

acme_dev: appreciated. Also flagging billing: our token rotation happened due to billing swap (different plan) — could that change caching/route? we saw slightly different backend pool on rotate.

raj_sre: routing change could switch to a backend that has older runtime binary; checking deploy history.

ingrid_runtime: good catch — two pools had different runtime versions; older one lacked terminal emission fix from previous minor. Hotfix will standardize behavior.

support_jen: I'll follow up when canary passes. For now customer asks for timeline to update their parser. propose message: "If you see EOF without final object, treat EOF as final after 1s and call /v1/stream/resume once with previous token." OK?

acme_dev: that works, we'll patch for now. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

ingrid_runtime: canary passed, rolling to 100% in 30m. PR: r/stream/fix-terminal-evt

support_jen: closing loop with customer after full deploy. tagging ticket INC-4521.
